messages:
lee: Heads-up — after the canary flip to sticky-routing we're seeing a weird dip in reported token credits for a subset of tenants, but actual infra usage is unchanged. anyone else seeing this?
anya: saw the spike in the dashboard. small group of routes (~12) show negative 'cache-savings' in the per-route card. :thinking: link: https://console/redwood/costs/route?range=1h
kevin: deploy-bot: canary/route-affinity v2 went live at 1734208000 — I don't think the canary itself changes accounting.
deploy-bot: canary deployed: canary-id=route-affinity-v2 env=prod shard=us-west-2
julia: my hunch is attribution mismatch: the amortized prefetch credits aren't being rolled up when sticky-routing pins a chain to a hot GPU. i.e. cache hits are real but our backend attribution logic isn't mapping to the new request meta.
kevin: confirmed — our econ-ingest events currently include: tenant_id, model_sku, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_hits, and request_ids. they do NOT include the routing affinity nor the active shard_id. that was deliberate to keep event cardinality low.
anya: we need route_affinity in the econ event to reconcile per-route amortized credits. otherwise the UI will keep showing phantom negative savings when a route gets pinned.
julia: agree but worried about cardinality explosion if we add full affinity strings. proposal: add an affinity_bucket (small int) generated at routing time, and include that in the event. buckets map to sticky groups, not full hostnames.
kevin: +1 for affinity_bucket. also suggest we add a lightweight hashed_shard (4 hex chars) and a boolean prefetch_owner flag. both are small and help joins.
lee: sample event sketch would help product and billing to validate.
kevin: posted a sample: ```json
{
  "tenant_id": "team-123",
  "model_sku": "open-8k-q4",
  "prompt_tokens": 48,
  "completion_tokens": 120,
  "cache_hits": 2,
  "affinity_bucket": 7,
  "hashed_shard": "a3f4",
  "prefetch_owner": false
}
```
anya: perfect. with affinity_bucket we can backfill the last 7 days by recomputing buckets from historical routing logs and stitching to econ events by request_id.
julia: backfill SQL (rough): ```sql
INSERT INTO econ_enriched (event_ts, tenant_id, model_sku, affinity_bucket)
SELECT e.ts, e.tenant_id, e.model_sku, hash_bucket(r.route_id, 16)
FROM econ_raw e
JOIN routing_logs r ON e.request_id = r.request_id
WHERE e.ts >= now() - interval '7 days';
```
kevin: note: hash_bucket is our deterministic function we've used elsewhere. backfill will be heavy — propose sampling first (10%) and comparing results before full run.
lee: UI ask: product wants a toggle in per-route cost card to view 'instant' vs 'amortized' savings so PMs can see before/after. adding affinity_bucket should let the view accurately show amortized prefetch credit across sticky groups.
anya: also request: telemetry team — please add an alert to notify when (amortized_savings < 0) for > 5 routes for 10m. that will catch regressions earlier. @kevin can you wire that?
kevin: will do. I'll open a small RFC: add affinity_bucket + hashed_shard + prefetch_owner to econ event schema, plus sampling backfill plan and performance guardrails. PR will include migration plan and dashboard toggle wireframe.
julia: one more ops note — make sure the new fields are optional in the ingest to avoid dropping old events; otherwise we'll create a v2 event and fragmentation will complicate backfills.
lee: agreed. action items: kevin opens RFC, anya drafts dashboard toggle UX, julia coordinates sampling backfill run, lee will create an oncall playbook for negative-savings alerts.
anya: timeline?
kevin: RFC by EOD today, sampling backfill Tuesday, UI toggle prototype Wednesday.
lee: sweet. thanks team :thumbsup:
anya: i'll schedule a 30m sync after RFC review.
lee: tagging @billing-team FYI — this will change how amortized preview numbers look in invoices during rollout.
kevin: noted. I'll add a migration note to changelog.
